html:
A philosopher, astronomer and mathematician of Alexandria in Roman Egypt, killed by a Christian mob in 415. She is the best-known woman scholar of the ancient world.

She was the daughter of the mathematician Theon, who produced the standard edition of Euclid's Elements, and she worked with him on texts of Ptolemy's astronomy. She wrote commentaries on advanced mathematics, now lost, and taught Neoplatonist philosophy to students both pagan and Christian, some of whom became bishops.

She was also a respected adviser to Orestes, the Roman governor of Egypt, who was locked in a feud with the city's bishop, Cyril. Rumours spread that she was blocking peace between them. In March 415 a mob of Christians dragged her from her carriage, killed her in a church and burned her remains.

Later writers turned her into a symbol of reason destroyed by fanaticism and of the end of ancient learning, sometimes linking her wrongly to the end of the Library of Alexandria. Her death was as much about city politics as about her ideas. The eastern Roman world went on studying Greek science after her.
sum: A philosopher, astronomer and mathematician of Alexandria in Roman Egypt, killed by a Christian mob in 415. She is the best-known woman scholar of the ancient world.
